2. The suit was filed by the plaintiff opposite party before the Court of Assistant Judge, Madaripur, for a declaration of his title in the suit land and also for a declaration that the memos dated 1.7.89 and 3.7.89 are illegal, void and without jurisdiction and also prayed for a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendant petitioner from realising tolls from the suit property. The plaintiff opposite party made an application under order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure for temporary injunction which was rejected by the Assistant Judge and on appeal the learned District judge allowed the appeal and granted temporary injunction against the defendant petitioner. Against that order of granting temporary injunction by the order dated 30.6.92, the present application under section 115 C.P.C. was filed and a Rule has been obtained. 

 3. The defendant petitioner asserts that the order dated 30.6.92 has been passed illegally when the learned Trial Court found that the plaintiff opposite parties to have no title and possession over the property from which the defendant petitioner has been injected. It is also the defendant petitioner's case that non-production of documents of title by the plaintiffs-opposite parties is a serious error, but the learned Judge has failed to consider it and in the face of no prima facie title and possession, the learned Judge illegally allowed the application for temporary injunction and as such the order dated 30.6.92 is liable to be set aside. 

 4. Perused the application and also heard the learned Advocates appearing for both the parties. The learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and order dated 6.4.91 found that due to change of the course of river Arial Kha the suit property as described in the schedule of the plaint is not an ascertained property properly bounded and butted and furthermore, the property being in possession of the defendant Pourashava, the Court refused to grant temporary injunction restraining the defendant petitioner from the suit land. The Appellate Court, on the other hand, has carefully considered the cases of the plaintiff as well as that of the defendant and found that the suit property was also a subject matter of litigation and by Title Suit No. 64 of 1966 the same has properly been established. The learned Judge reproduced the decree passed in Title suit No. 64 of 1966. The settlement sheet granted in favour of the plaintiffs shows the schedule property as follows:- 

 7. Thus it appears that the learned Judge on due application of his judicial mind of the facts and circumstances of the case reversed the judgment and order of the trial Court and granted temporary injunction restraining the defendants from causing interference by finding that the plaintiff has a prima facie case and that by the settlement which covers a period from 1350 B.S. to 1405 B.S., the plaintiff has title and possession over the suit property for half a century this finding is a question of fact. The Court of appeal being the last Court of fact, it is difficult to interfere with the finding of fact arrived by the last Court of fact. The learned Judge found that Bhasan Mahol as described in the settlement sheet existed in the same place after lapse of 45 years on account of continuous change of the course of river. This is a question of fact settled by the last Court of fact. I find nothing to interfere with such a finding of fact upon which the learned Judge found a prima facie case of the plaintiff and allowed temporary injunction. The judgment and order dated 30.6.92 passed by the learned District Judge calls for no interference.
